newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm after rangebound session.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm after rangebound session.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended slightly firmer on Tuesday after an uneventful session in which the contract was trapped in a range of just over $1.00.
August ended 75 cents up at $167.75 a tonne, having failed to breach resistance at $168. September crude was trading 13 cents up at $18.54 a barrel, off a high of $18.65.
The whole complex was tracking moves on NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures, brokers said.
NYMEX August gasoline, which expires on Thursday, dipped off highs but was trading nearly one cent a gallon higher in the first hour of trade.
The U.S. gasoline market has been buoyed recently by tight supplies of methyl tertiary butane ether (MTBE).
MTBE is a key blending component used in converting conventional unleaded to reformulated gasoline, the grade deliverable against the NYMEX contract.
"Gasoline is the main leader at the moment," said one broker.

News that Exxon Corp had shut its 110,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker at its 411,000 bpd Baytown, Texas refinery after a lightening strike encouraged more short-covering on gasoline, brokers said.
"No-one wants to be short ahead of the APIs," another broker said.

Traders were expecting weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), due after the close of trade, to show a draw on gasoline stocks of between one and three million barrels and a slight rise in distillate stocks.
